assumption: Active 18-34s want an after-training snack that is low in sugar AND made from real food (not just one of the two)
current_evidence: Founder reports people 'said yes to the idea' (unquantified); competitor map shows the gap exists (EVIDENCE: 02) but not that people want it
cheapest_test: Upload 9 interview notes + 20 more past-behaviour interviews; ask what they avoid in bars and why
metric: % who unprompted mention sugar, sweeteners or 'processed' as a reason to avoid bars

assumption: ~14 g protein is enough (buyers won't insist on 20 g)
current_evidence: Lab bars set a 20 g norm (EVIDENCE: 02); untested with our buyers
cheapest_test: Taste test + pilot survey: 'Would you want more protein even if it meant protein powder?'

assumption: People will pay ~£2.75 for a 90 g fresh bake
cheapest_test: Waitlist price question + pilot sales at £2.75

assumption: Buyers repeat-purchase (it's not a one-off novelty)
cheapest_test: Paid pilot at 2 partners over 3 weeks

assumption: A chilled product with a ~3-day use-by works for partners (fridge space, low waste)
cheapest_test: Ask partners in pilot chats; count waste in pilot
metric: Partners with fridge space; % of delivered bars wasted

assumption: The bar tastes good without dates/honey (only banana for sweetness)
cheapest_test: Blind taste test vs Grenade and Forza (n~20)

assumption: The calculated numbers (~3 g sugar, ~14 g protein, ~28 g carbs per 90 g) hold in a real bake
current_evidence: Calculation with typical values; 24% bake loss assumed (04-nutrition.py)
cheapest_test: Weigh before/after baking (free) + 1 lab nutrition analysis
metric: Lab sugar and protein vs calc
success_threshold: Sugar <=4.5 g/100 g (keeps 'low sugar'); protein >=12 g/bar

assumption: Home-baked bars come out consistent (weight, texture) bake to bake
cheapest_test: Weigh 8 bars from each of 3 bakes

assumption: Clubs and gyms will stock or bulk-buy (Squad Box)
current_evidence: Pro clubs tied to SiS/Myprotein/Grenade (inherited); grassroots untested
metric: Partners agreeing to a pilot; reorder intent

assumption: The use-by period agreed with the EHO is at least 3 days
cheapest_test: Fridge keep test days 1/3/5/7 + ask EHO

assumption: 'fettle' is free to use as a trade mark in classes 29/30
current_evidence: No clash found by web search; UK IPO not checked
cheapest_test: UK IPO + Companies House search (30 min)

assumption: A local bakery could bake it under contract at <=£0.90/bar

current_evidence: Claims checked vs GB register conditions; wording untested

assumption: ~5-6 g fibre straight after training causes no meaningful gut discomfort
